checks.claim: Parent application: Proposition 22.8 with h=V_sigma, g=0 gives the actual physical F flow; finite horizons and autonomy give all t>=0.
checks.reason: A time-constant V_sigma lies in C([0,T];C_c^infinity(K)). At g=0 the driver is the Lipschitz primitive A_h, so it is C^theta with A_h(0)=0. Proposition 22.4 gives U, and Lemma 22.6's Riemann-sum argument, carried over by Proposition 22.8, gives the statewise F Duhamel equation with iB_F(V). The force is +V u, so H=-Delta-V, which agrees with (1.1). Picard uniqueness gives overlap compatibility and P(t,s)=P(t-s,0). Proposition 22.5 and S_F(t)iE=iE give invariance of iE, so the E restriction solves E Duhamel. No uniform-horizon stochastic statement is used.

checks.claim: Primary pins: Teschl second edition, Theorems 10.2 and 10.13, Theorem 4.12 and Corollary 4.13, with correct hypotheses, pages and order of use.
checks.reason: The title page, copyright page (ISBN 978-1-4704-1704-8, GSM 157, copyright 2009, 2014) and printed pages 140, 141, 258 and 273 match every citation. Theorem 10.2: a real potential in L^infty_infty+L^2 for n<=3 gives self-adjoint H0+V on H^2, bounded below, ess spec [0,infinity), C_c^infinity core. Theorem 10.13 is conditional on the bottom being an eigenvalue, and the note invokes it only after the trial and threshold argument. Theorem 4.12 allows the form domain and sets E_n=inf ess spec once eigenvalues end. H0=-Delta. The source is not credited with uniformity, F projection or moments. Note: the phrase 'form monotonicity' slightly glosses Corollary 4.13, whose printed form is A>=B, A-B>=0; the proof does not depend on it.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.1, form domain: H^1 is the common form domain, c=1+M, A>=1, with displayed norm bounds.
checks.reason: On H^2, ||A^{1/2}u||^2=q(u)+c||u||^2=||u||_{H1}^2+int(M-V)|u|^2, using 0<=V<=M, which gives the bounds with constants 1 and c. Spectral cutoffs give a form core, Fourier cutoffs give H^1 density, and both norms dominate L^2, so the completions coincide with the same limits.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.1, ground state: trial first, then eigenvalue, then simplicity and positivity; E2 convention; Lipschitz levels; rate gap.
checks.reason: -M<=E1<=-epsilon holds by Rayleigh on the common H^1. The bottom lies in the spectrum and below the essential threshold 0, hence is an isolated finite-multiplicity eigenvalue, and only then is 10.13 invoked. The E2 convention matches Teschl's. E1<E2<=0 holds. |q_sigma-q_tau|<=d_V on common unit tests gives (23.3) through identical sup/inf sets, including the threshold case. lambda-mu=(E2-E1)/(lambda+mu) with lambda+mu<=2 sqrt M, and lambda+mu>=sqrt epsilon>0 makes the denominator nonzero; there is no division by mu.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.1, L2 and H2 continuity of the ground state.
checks.reason: a=<p_sigma,p_tau> lies in (0,1] by a.e. positivity. q_sigma(p_tau)=a^2 E1+q_sigma(r)>=E1+Delta_*||r||^2 and q_sigma(p_tau)<=E1+2 d_V. Then ||p_tau-p_sigma||^2=2(1-a)<=2(1-a^2)=2||r||^2<=4 d_V/Delta_*. The sign in (1-Delta)p=(1-lambda^2+V)p is correct. 1+2M is a valid, crude L^2 bound, since |1-lambda^2+V|<=1+2M. The Bessel inverse is an isometry. No p in L1 or ODE input appears.

checks.claim: Lemma 23.2: resolvent supremum, order reversal, square-root integral, quarter-power norms, negative entry.
checks.reason: Completing the square gives <f,(T+t)^{-1}f>=sup{2Re<f,u>-q_T(u)-t||u||^2}. The order reversal and I-t(T+t)^{-1} monotonicity are correct. Substituting t=x r^2 gives sqrt x=(1/pi) int t^{-1/2} x/(x+t) dt. Tonelli in the extended sense gives T^{1/2}<=S^{1/2} with domain inclusions, with no general power monotonicity assumed. From B<=A<=cB: ||A^{1/4}u||^2<=c^{1/2}||B^{1/4}u||^2, hence constant c^{1/4} in (23.6). The dual norm is attained at a multiple of A^{-1/2}z, and the dual comparison gives ||A^{-1/4}z||<=||B^{-1/4}z||<=c^{1/4}||A^{-1/4}z||, uniformly in sigma on all of R^d.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.3: C_t,S_t definitions, balanced entries, high and low frequency, mu=0, complement bound.
checks.reason: The definitions on h>0, h=0, h<0 are correct. Conjugating by (A^{1/4},A^{-1/4}) gives C, sqrt(h+c)S, -hS/sqrt(h+c), C. For h>=0: |S|<=min(t,h^{-1/2}), the upper entry is <=sqrt(1+c)(1+t), and the lower entry is <=1. For -mu^2<=h<0: cosh<=e^{mu t}, sinh(ty)/y<=t e^{mu t}, |h|<=M, and h+c lies in [1,c]. The spectrum on the complement of p is at or above E2, including threshold and mu=0.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.3: both ground branches, decaying mode retained in I-Pi, bounded projections, eigen-relations.
checks.reason: Pi^E plus the decaying projection equals the spatial projection on both entries. ell(e)=1. c-lambda^2 lies in [1,c] and lambda>=sqrt epsilon give uniform projection norms in the spectral norm. Direct computation gives cosh+sinh=e^{lambda t} on (p,lambda p) and (a+b/lambda)'=lambda(a+b/lambda) for the left eigenrelation. The decaying branch is bounded and absorbed into C(1+t)e^{mu t}. Pairings are continuous since p is in H^2.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.3: identification of the spectral matrix with the actual physical E flow, including real subspace.
checks.reason: The graph-level weights produce the same balanced entries. ||Au|| and ||Bu|| are equivalent with constant 1+M since A-B=M-V lies in [0,M]. u is in C^1(H^1) and C(H^2), z is in C^1(L^2) and C(H^1). The free group on H^1xL^2 has c=1 weighted entries bounded by C(1+T) and generator (z,Delta u) with domain H^2xH^1. The product rule gives force (z,Delta u+Vu)-(z,Delta u)=(0,Vu). The identity embeds into E. Multiplication V: H^{1/2} to H^{-1/2} has bound M, so Picard uniqueness applies. Density within E only, with boundedness of both operators. Real potentials make the functional calculus preserve real phases. The free matrix agrees with S from Lemma 22.1.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.4: triangular block, forcing convolution, E-valued Fubini.
checks.reason: The force splits as B_F(V)(Y,C(r)c)=B^E Y+D C(r)c. The triangle exchange is correct and absolute on a finite triangle with jointly strongly continuous integrand. Y solves free Duhamel with force B^E Y+g. With the constant block this is the F Duhamel equation, so uniqueness gives (23.11). The c1 and c2 columns are both retained through C(r). Uniform finite-horizon bounds follow from ||B_F(V)||<=||V||_infty+||V||_2.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.4: f, both dual constants, tail identity, rank-one normalization, commutation, continuity, positive margins.
checks.reason: ell^E D C(r)c=f(c1+r c2) with f=int V p/(2 lambda). The integral int_0^infty e^{-lambda r}f(c1+r c2)dr=f(c1/lambda+c2/lambda^2) is correct. The tail integral equals ell^C(C(t)c) by r=t+s. Finite integral plus tail gives ell P(t)=e^{lambda t}ell. ell(e_sigma)=1. Commutation (23.14) follows. f>0 since (23.1) forces V nonzero, V>=0, p>0 a.e.; finiteness is by L2 Cauchy-Schwarz. ell(e_0)=f/lambda for e_0=(0,1,0), and O_phi(e_sigma)=int phi p>0. Continuity on compact I gives (23.15). All continuity uses H^2 continuity of p and the rate floor.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.5: exact complement including minus e^E ell^C(C(t)c), polynomial, normalized exponential.
checks.reason: Q(e,c) has E part Q^E e-e^E ell^C(c). Substituting into (23.11) and splitting D gives exactly (23.19) by the tail identity. int_0^t(1+t-r)(1+r)dr=t+t^2+t^3/6 was verified by hand. The first term is C(1+t)e^{mu t}, the final and constant terms are C(1+t)|c|, the total is C(1+t)^3 e^{mu t} since mu>=0, and multiplying by e^{-lambda t} gives C_eta e^{-eta t} for eta<d0.

checks.claim: Proposition 23.5: parameter bound by statewise Duhamel, measurability and Gronwall.
checks.reason: The difference decomposition is correct. ||B_sigma-B_tau||<=||dV||_infty+||dV||_2 follows from Lemma 22.3's bound. The operator norm is a countable supremum of continuous functions by separability from Lemma 22.1. Scalar Gronwall needs no operator-norm continuity of S_F or operator-valued derivative.

checks.claim: Lemma 23.6: original raw mean, variance, positivity, floors, smoothness, for all nonseparable Psi, with Gamma once.
checks.reason: The pairing follows from (1.2)-type covariance with compact tests, locally finite Gamma and a<1. Gamma appears once, in h. v=int Psi h. Spatial bound ||Psi||^2|B_A|Gamma(closed B_{2A}), since |z|<2A. int int |sigma-u|^{-a}=2/((1-a)(2-a)) verified. Homogeneity gives Gamma(B_1)=r^{alpha-d}Gamma(B_r). Autocorrelation is positive near 0, so 0<Q<infty. |sigma-u|^{-a}>=1 on the unit square gives h>=Gamma*qbar on I and v>=Q(qbar). With r=s-u derivatives fall on the zero-extended smooth Psi, so joint smoothness holds. Separability, a global decay assumption and a masked raw covariance are all absent, and the white and invariant-direction cases are covered. Note: 'every positive-radius ball' must be read as origin-centered (see minor findings); the actual use is origin-centered.

checks.reason: ||psi_L||_2=1. Kinetic energy D_psi L^-2. psi_L^2>=c0^2 L^-d on B_L. Tonelli gives int_{B_L}Gamma*qbar=int qbar(y)Gamma(B_L-y)dy. B_{L/2} is contained in B_L-y for |y|<=A<=L/2.
